## Answer: 16

**Upper bound.** Suppose a colour class $C$ satisfies the condition. Every cell of $C$ has at least two neighbours in $C$, so the subgraph of the grid induced by $C$ has minimum degree at least 2. A finite graph with minimum degree at least 2 contains a cycle. The grid graph is bipartite, so every cycle has even length, and it has no triangles, so every cycle has length at least 4. Hence each colour class contains at least 4 cells. With 64 cells, the number of colours is at most $64/4 = 16$.

**Construction.** Split the board into sixteen disjoint $2\times 2$ blocks and give each block its own colour. Every cell in a block has exactly two edge-neighbours inside its block, both of the same colour, so the condition holds for all cells. This uses 16 colours.

Therefore the maximum is 16.

ANSWER: 16
